readings.what: every name @oimdb/core exports, re-exported so nothing is droppable
new OIMDB() and nothing else — the toll every consumer pays
a database, a population, a write, a subscription and a read — no index at all
the same consumer, holding the four grouping bodies a method form would have given it
the same consumer, taking groupBy alone and reading one unordered group
the same caller, holding the three groupings one shared module could not withhold
the same caller, holding the ordered mutator an `order?` ternary would have named

findings.question: Is the bundler dropping code nothing reaches?
findings.requirement: a database alone under 60% of the whole surface
findings.caveat: An application that constructs a database and touches nothing else must not carry the hundred modules of the published surface. If this reads near 1.00 the bundler kept everything, every arm below is the same bundle under four names, and every difference in this report is a rounding of zero — including the one it was written to settle, which would then read as "the ordered-list diff is free". That is a conclusion this project would enjoy and has not earned, so it voids the report instead.

findings.question: Is the minifier running at all?
findings.requirement: minified under 70% of the same bundle unminified
findings.caveat: This package ships roughly as many bytes of comment as of code, and a claim about what is SHIPPED is a claim about output a minifier has already been through. If these two numbers are equal the minifier did nothing, and every kilobyte below is mostly prose — in the direction that flatters the decision the claim defends, which is the one to guard hardest.

findings.question: What would the grouping layer cost an application that never groups anything, if the four groupings hung off the collection class as methods?
findings.requirement: none — this row is the measurement, not an attestation
findings.caveat: THE DECISION THIS ROW PRICES IS `packaging.a-grouping-is-a-free-function`. Every consumer of this library holds a POPULATION; a bundler cannot drop a class's methods one at a time; so under the method form the arm on the left would have carried everything the arm on the right carries — the four grouping bodies and every address store, membership source and mutator they name — without a line of the application being able to reach any of it. WHAT THE ARM ON THE RIGHT STANDS IN FOR: the four names are pushed rather than written as four method bodies inside `OIMCollection`, which loses the method form four function signatures and four module wrappers — tens of bytes in ITS favour, against a closure both forms carry identically. The decomposition below names that closure module by module, so the claim can be checked rather than believed. PREDICTED ≈14.8 KB minified, by adding up module sizes in the ordered-list artifact — arithmetic over an artifact, not a measurement, stated here so this run either confirms or refutes it.

findings.question: What would one shared grouping module cost a caller who takes exactly one grouping?
findings.requirement: none — this row is the measurement, not an attestation
findings.caveat: THE DECISION THIS ROW PRICES IS `packaging.each-grouping-is-its-own-module-with-its-own-memo`. A module exporting four INDEPENDENT functions would shake per export and this row would read near zero — that is not the design that was turned down. The one turned down is a single module over ONE memo keyed by the columns and a token saying which grouping it was, so one mint-and-memo helper serves all four shapes, and a helper branching over a token names every address store and every membership source from one function body. A bundler cannot see past a runtime test. WHAT THE ARM ON THE RIGHT STANDS IN FOR, and the direction it errs: the other three groupings are pushed rather than routed through a shared helper, so the shared form would write the mint scaffolding once instead of four times and save whatever that scaffolding costs while still dragging every strategy — this row is an UPPER BOUND, and the strategies are the kilobytes. THE REACHABILITY HALF IS NOT MEASURED HERE AND IS NOT OPEN: `packages/core/tests/what-an-import-retains.test.ts` already asserts, with no toolchain, that `groupBy` retains none of `OIMBucketAddressStoreByIdentityChain`, `OIMMembershipSourceDerivedMany` or `OIMMembershipSourceAll`. PREDICTED ≈4.5 KB minified for four grouping modules rather than one, by arithmetic over the ordered-list artifact rather than by a build — stated here so this run answers it.

findings.question: What would an `order?` option cost a caller who groups one column and sorts nothing?
findings.requirement: none — this row is the measurement, not an attestation
findings.caveat: THE DECISION THIS ROW PRICES IS `packaging.a-grouping-takes-a-constructed-mutator`. Under the shipped design the mutator arrives constructed, so `groupBy` names exactly one mutator — the unordered fallback. Under the option form it names both arms of `order === undefined ? new OIMBucketMutatorUnordered() : new OIMBucketMutatorOrdered(order)`, and a bundler cannot see past a runtime test, so the ordered mutator and the two modules only it reaches follow every consumer who groups ANYTHING. WHAT THE ARM ON THE RIGHT STANDS IN FOR: the class is referenced and never constructed, which is faithful — retention is decided by a live symbol naming the class, not by the `new` running — but the ternary itself and the option plumbing are absent, a few dozen bytes in the option form's favour that are NOT subtracted. THE REACHABILITY HALF IS ALREADY PINNED by `what-an-import-retains.test.ts`, whose own title says it: "the mutator is an argument, not an option". PREDICTED ≈5.6 KB minified, by arithmetic over the ordered-list artifact rather than by a build.
